newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil CVRD April 29 auction date maintained.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil CVRD April 29 auction date maintained.

text.p: Brazil will push ahead with the planned April 29 privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD despite a high court injunction against the government.

The injunction granted Tuesday by Supreme Court Justice Marco Aurelio de Mello suspended the transfer to CVRD of 411,000 hectares of mineral properties in the Carajas mining area in the northern Brazilian state of Para.
In comments to reporters Mello said his injunction would not oblige the government to suspend the privatization auction, but suggested it would make it pointless.

However, Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees the privatization process, is appealing the ruling by the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) and is adamant the auction will not be delayed.
"We will appeal this decision, but it does not affect the auction scheduled for April 29," BNDES Vice-President Jose Pio Borges told reporters.
He said the injunction did not affect the economic value of CVRD's mining and exploration rights.
Under Brazilian legislation, a company may be entitled to explore and mine in a given area, even if the property and the right to use the land above ground belongs to a third party, Borges said.
The injunction, sought by opposition lawmakers, still needs to be approved by the full STF. The date for a hearing by the high court has still not been set.
In a statement, the STF said that, under the constitution, Congress must approve any concession over 2,500 hectares by the president.

The 411,000 hectares in the Carajas mining area, home to the largest iron ore deposit in the world, were transfered in a presidential decree signed by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso March 6, the same day tender documents for the CVRD sale were published.

Carajas is CVRD's main mining asset and the prize investors are seeking in their bid to acquire the 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD which is being sold off April 29 for a base price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).

A Planning Ministry spokeswoman said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir did not believe the court injunction would affect the interest shown by consortia intending to bid for the CVRD stake. An expected bidder in the auction declined to comment on the ruling.
More than 60 lawsuits have been filed against the privatization of CVRD, but the BNDES is confident it can fight off any legal challenges to the sell-off successfully.

The CVRD sell-off is Latin America's largest privatization to date and is expected to net the government at least $5 billion, that is $2 billion more than the region's previous record privatization of Argentine oil firm YPF.

CVRD shares on the Sao Paulo stock exchange fell sharply on news of the court injunction. CVRD's prefered blue chip closed down 1.34 percent at 25.75 reais, but had been down even more during the afternoon.
